sources.title: Republic of Marshall Islands Climate Security Risk Assessment
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), with IOM and Adelphi under the Climate Security in the Pacific project
sources.temporal_coverage: 2023 assessment drawing on earlier historical evidence and climate projections, including scenarios to 2050 and 2080.
sources.methodology: Climate models, literature review, stakeholder consultations and interviews.
sources.limitations: Living, non-exhaustive assessment; projections carry stated uncertainty.

sources.title: National Adaptation Plan Community Engagement Summary Report: Majuro Atoll
sources.organization: International Organization for Migration (IOM), engaged by the Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands
sources.temporal_coverage: Majuro NAP consultations conducted October 2022-May 2023; report cover dated 2023.
sources.methodology: Majuro summary of surveys, Day-in-Life activities, focus groups, interviews and community profiles.
sources.limitations: Consultation findings are participant observations, not representative prevalence or causal estimates.

sources.title: Implementation Status & Results Report: Pacific Resilience Project II under the Pacific Resilience Program (P160096)
sources.temporal_coverage: Project implementation status through 28 February 2025, with a World Bank mission update dated 15 April 2025.
sources.methodology: World Bank implementation-status report using project indicators and implementation updates.
sources.limitations: Agency-reported outputs and progress; no independent outcome evaluation was reviewed.

sources.title: Coastal Risk Assesment for Ebeye
sources.organization: Global Facility for Disaster Reduction and Recovery (GFDRR), World Bank
sources.temporal_coverage: GFDRR technical-report summary published 22 June 2018; assessment tests coastal hazards and climate/sea-level scenarios.
sources.methodology: GFDRR landing-page summary of a coastal hazard and risk assessment.
sources.limitations: The linked 17.8 MB technical-report PDF could not be retrieved; only the opened landing-page summary supports claims.

claims.locator: PDF p.6, lines on inundation, Ajeltake-Laura access and groups lacking support
claims.paraphrase: In Majuro, inundation disrupts livelihoods and can block Ajeltake-Laura youth from school or town; women, youth and disabled residents reported inadequate high-tide support.
affected_groups: persons with physical or mental disabilities
claims.limitations: Summary of consultation observations, not measured population-wide access rates.

claims.locator: PDF p.6, women participants' report on heat, socializing, abuse and gender-based violence
claims.paraphrase: Majuro women reported heat-related declines in socializing and increased abuse and gender-based violence.
claims.limitations: Consultation account, not a prevalence estimate.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Women explicitly linked heat with more abuse and gender-based violence.

claims.locator: PDF p.8, Chamber of Commerce consultation on land tenure and flood-proofing incentives
claims.paraphrase: Majuro business participants said leasehold land weakens incentives to invest in flood-proofing buildings that eventually revert to landlords.
claims.limitations: Consultation participants' account, not a representative business survey.

claims.locator: PDF p.11, community solidarity and adaptation-asset findings; PDF p.12, proposed actions
claims.paraphrase: Participants reported food/water sharing and cleanups; the report identifies solidarity and cooperation as a climate-response asset.
claims.limitations: Self-reported practices, not an outcome evaluation.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report calls social cohesion an adaptation asset.

claims.locator: PDF p.7, Day-in-Life survey on planned adaptation or migration after an extreme sea-level scenario briefing
claims.paraphrase: Most consulted Majuro participants favored in-place adaptation; 10% of Day-in-Life respondents considered migration after an extreme sea-level briefing.
claims.scenario: Extreme sea-level scenario was described in the briefing; no modeled pathway was specified.
claims.limitations: Intentions, not observed migration or a forecast.

claims.locator: PDF p.23, drought projections for southern atolls and uncertainty note
claims.paraphrase: The assessment cites a greater likelihood of severe drought in southern atolls by 2050 under RCP8.5, while flagging high uncertainty.
claims.scenario: RCP8.5; the report states projection uncertainty is high.
claims.limitations: The report says model uncertainty is high and some rainfall-based drought projections differ.

claims.locator: PDF p.29, land insecurity section on relocation, private land and possible government-landowner friction
claims.paraphrase: With no public land, climate relocation may cause friction between landowners and government.
claims.scenario: Conditional risk; no climate scenario or date stated.
claims.limitations: Potential friction, not a documented dispute.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Report warns relocation may cause landowner-government friction.

claims.locator: PDF pp.35-36, internal migration section on environmental stress, crowding, resource competition and discontent
claims.paraphrase: The report links environmental stress and outer-island food/water insecurity to movement toward crowded Majuro/Ebeye, potentially raising resource competition and discontent.
claims.scenario: Conditional pathway; no emissions scenario or date specified.
claims.limitations: Potential pathway, not a causal forecast.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: It links climate stress, migration and possible urban discontent.

claims.locator: PDF p.55, Entry Point 4 on customary knowledge, resource pressures and conflict resolution
claims.paraphrase: UNDP recommends outer-island investment, community disaster training, early warning and customary knowledge, including traditional conflict-resolution practices.
claims.limitations: Recommendations and entry points, not evaluated or funded outcomes.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report says customary knowledge can support resilience and resolve conflicts linked to resource and livelihood stress.

claims.locator: PDF p.2, implementation status: emergency communication installations and operator training completed January 2025
claims.paraphrase: The report records 63 emergency communication stations completed and 1,369 operators trained across 63 communities, including 550 women, by January 2025.
hazards: hazards covered by emergency communication network
claims.limitations: Project-reported activity and reach, not evidence of reduced disaster losses.

claims.locator: PDF p.6, project indicator notes on national and local climate/disaster working groups operationalized
claims.paraphrase: By February 2025, national and local climate/disaster working groups had been operationalized, and the National Adaptation Plan incorporated coastal vulnerability assessment results.
claims.limitations: World Bank project reporting; does not evaluate the groups' effectiveness.

claims.locator: PDF pp.2 and 4, April 2025 mission status on Ebeye seawall mobilization and construction schedule
claims.paraphrase: At the April 2025 mission, the Ebeye seawall contractor was mobilized and works were reported on schedule; protection outcomes were not yet reported.
claims.limitations: April 2025 status only; no later construction or effectiveness result was reviewed.

claims.locator: GFDRR landing page, technical-report summary on assessed islands, hazards and risk-analysis scope
claims.paraphrase: GFDRR says the assessment analyzed waves, storm surges, typhoons and tsunamis for Majuro and Ebeye, with detailed inundation and erosion risk analysis for Ebeye.
claims.limitations: This claim reflects the opened publisher summary, not inspection of the full technical report.

access_audit.locator: Full 68-page PDF inspected; especially PDF pp.12-16, 23-27, 29-36 and 52-58.
access_audit.notes: Assessment combines models, literature and consultations; pathway statements are identified as risks, not country-specific causal estimates.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrase only.

access_audit.locator: Full 15-page Majuro community-engagement summary inspected, especially PDF pp.6-8 and 11-12.
access_audit.notes: The document summarizes 2022-23 consultations in Majuro; findings are not national prevalence estimates.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrase only.

access_audit.locator: Full 11-page implementation-status report inspected, especially PDF pp.2 and 5-8.
access_audit.notes: Performance statements retain the report's February and April 2025 dates; no post-report outcome is inferred.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrase only.

access_audit.locator: Opened GFDRR landing-page report summary, especially lines 184-194.
access_audit.notes: The summary is direct publisher text; the linked technical report was not accessed and is not paraphrased beyond this summary.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrase only.

access_audit.locator: GFDRR Download link returned a content-size retrieval error for the 17.8 MB technical PDF.
access_audit.notes: No full-report claims were made; only the opened landing-page summary is used.

access_audit.locator: The national NAP PDF timed out during retrieval; its search-result text was not used as evidence.
access_audit.notes: Subnational claims instead rely on the opened Majuro consultation summary and other full-text sources.

access_audit.locator: IOM-hosted 36-page national community-consultation report returned 403; alternate Monash PDF also failed retrieval.
access_audit.notes: No claims were taken from search excerpts; use is limited to the separately opened 15-page Majuro summary report.

search_audit.query: Marshall Islands named districts and communities exposed to climate hazards, flooding, drought, water and service disruption
search_audit.outcome: Opened reports identify named vulnerability in Majuro/Ajeltake-Laura and Ebeye, with broader southern/northern atoll patterns; this review does not provide complete island-by-island coverage.

search_audit.query: Marshall Islands source-stated climate links to gender-based violence, land insecurity, resource competition and migration
search_audit.outcome: UNDP identifies conditional landowner-government friction and mobility/resource-competition risks; Majuro women participants reported heat-related abuse/GBV. These are source-stated risks or consultations, not proof of violence causation.

search_audit.query: Marshall Islands insecurity, land tenure, institutions or violence that may impede climate adaptation and access to services
search_audit.outcome: No reviewed source documents armed conflict or organized insecurity blocking a named adaptation project. Consultation findings identify leasehold disincentives to flood-proofing and access/support barriers for vulnerable groups.

search_audit.query: Marshall Islands local adaptation capacity, community knowledge, emergency warnings, disaster response and coastal protection results
search_audit.outcome: IOM records community solidarity and proposed water/disability actions; UNDP recommends customary knowledge and conflict resolution; the World Bank reports trained communication operators, operationalized coordination groups and dated Ebeye seawall progress.

gaps: The national RMI NAP PDF and 36-page My Heritage Is Here consultation report could not be opened; indexed text from those inaccessible documents was excluded.
The full Ebeye coastal-risk technical report was too large to retrieve; the single claim uses only the official GFDRR landing-page summary.
The accessed community consultation summary covers Majuro only; the assessed northern and southern atoll patterns do not constitute comprehensive subnational coverage.
The direct climate-FCV claims are conditional risks or participant reports; no countrywide causal estimate or observed violence escalation is established.
No reviewed source documents organized conflict blocking a named climate-adaptation intervention; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
World Bank project outputs and April 2025 seawall progress are historical by the 2026 review date; no later completion/effectiveness report was accessed.
